doc.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Singing with Goodman, and bandleaders using their players
summary: Goodman let him sing, Kenton did not; they wrote a song with Flip Phillips, and Goodman and Ellington make shows from their players.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Benny Goodman let me start singing. Now Stan Kenton wouldn’t let me sing because he thought I would say something off color, so he would watch me closely.
Oh I can’t imagine you saying anything off color, come on.

I can’t either but I mean Stan was worried that I might. I don’t know where he got that idea. But Benny, you know Benny didn’t care. I took Benny Goodman to see Lenny Bruce one time, and I said, “What did you think, Benny?” And he said, “He’s skating on thin ice.” Benny was a very clever guy. I loved Benny Goodman. And so I forget what we were talking about.
We were talking about the vocal thing.

Oh yeah. So we were working in Atlantic City and Flip Phillips and I wrote a song, called “My Baby Done Told Me.” And we had a little arrangement and everything. And it’s recorded on some album — some album made in Europe when we were over there. So I started singing with his band and pretty soon that was part of the show. Benny was a great band leader because he’d take whatever band he had and make a show out of it, where this guy would have his number. We had Red Norvo and Jerry Dodgion and Bill © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
Harris and Flip Phillips. So it had a lot of little stuff inside the band. We’d have a great little show.
And Benny, he was good at doing that. Well I guess all the real good band leaders, like Duke Ellington, that’s the way he does it too, he uses everybody to their—
Yeah, he’d write to their sound and their personality.
Yeah. Use everybody to the hilt.
Yeah. Of course you have to be flexible though, because the next time out you might not have the same people and you have to have that ability to tailor the music to the players I guess.
